{{short description|Luger and physicist}}
'''George Franklin Tucker''' (born December 15, 1947, in [[San Juan, Puerto Rico]]<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/tu/george-tucker-1.html "George Tucker"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090406004826/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/tu/george-tucker-1.html |date=April 6, 2009 }}, Sports References</ref>) is a [[Puerto Rico|Puerto Rican]] [[physicist]] and former [[Olympic Games|Olympic]] [[luge]]r.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breaking News, Analysis, Politics, Blogs, News Photos, Video, Tech Reviews - TIME.com |url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,966821-1,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025144249/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,966821-1,00.html |archive-date=2012-10-25 |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=TIME.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

He [[Puerto Rico at the 1984 Winter Olympics|represented Puerto Rico]] in the [[Luge at the 1984 Winter Olympics – Men's singles|luge]] event at the [[1984 Winter Olympics]] in [[Sarajevo]], and was the only Puerto Rican representative at the Games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olympics Site Closed {{!}} Olympics at Sports-Reference.com |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics.html |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=www.sports-reference.com}}</ref> He was also the country's flagbearer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breaking News, Analysis, Politics, Blogs, News Photos, Video, Tech Reviews - TIME.com |url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,921573-2,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025144314/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,921573-2,00.html |archive-date=2012-10-25 |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=TIME.com |language=en-us}}</ref> Tucker was, at the time, a [[doctorate|doctoral student]] at [[Wesleyan University]] in the [[United States]]. He was later described by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' as "overweight but quick-witted" and as "the press's favorite loser". He finished last in his event, and reportedly "got a lot more press in the States than [[Paul Hildgartner]], the Italian who won the gold medal".<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20121203015800/http://vault.sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1066996/index.htm|title="Losers Of Renown"}}, ''Sports Illustrated'', January 27, 1988</ref> He described himself as "the luger who dripped blood", and ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' reported that he "shed alarming amounts of skin bouncing off the wall".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breaking News, Analysis, Politics, Blogs, News Photos, Video, Tech Reviews - TIME.com |url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,966821-1,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025144249/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,966821-1,00.html |archive-date=2012-10-25 |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=TIME.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

Tucker represented [[Puerto Rico at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Puerto Rico]] again at the [[1988 Winter Olympics]] in [[Calgary]],<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/tu/george-tucker-1.html "George Tucker"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090406004826/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/tu/george-tucker-1.html |date=April 6, 2009 }}, Sports References</ref> but was, this time, one of nine Puerto Rican competitors.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/PUR/winter/1988/ "Puerto Rico at the 1988 Calgary Winter Games"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110519161928/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/PUR/winter/1988/ |date=May 19, 2011 }}, Sports References</ref> Tucker competed in the luge with teammate [[Raúl Muñiz]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Janofsky |first1=Michael |last2=Thomas |first2=Robert Mcg. Jr |title=Being There |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=January 18, 1988 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/01/18/sports/sports-world-specials-being-there.html}}</ref> This time, he did not finish last.<ref name=NYT-2017-11-17>{{cite news |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2017/11/17/sports/olympics/nigeria-has-an-olympic-bobsled-team-and-tonga-had-a-luger.html |title= Nigeria Has an Olympic-Level Bobsled Team, and Tonga Had a Luger |author= Victor Mather |date= 17 November 2017 |work= New York Times }}</ref>

According to Puerto Rican bobsled coach Rich Kolko, Tucker in 1984 "set the standard for Caribbean nations competing" in Winter sports – such as the [[Jamaican bobsled team]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Eskenazi |first=Gerald |title=Olympics: Five days to Albertville; Sledding Controversy Leads to Compensation |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=February 3, 1992 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/02/03/sports/olympics-five-days-to-albertville-sledding-controversy-leads-to-compensation.html}}</ref>
